cards.subject: Franclorn Forgewright's spire
lines: Blackrock Spire was designed by a master Dark Iron mason to be the symbol of dwarven power in this mountain.
Hordemar City is built inside the husk of it. The walls around the orc tents are carved out of volcanic rock — dwarf work, not orc work. The orcs pitched campfires in somebody else's stone rooms.

cards.subject: It is a ten-man dungeon
lines: Blackrock Spire launched as a raid instance. Patch 1.3.0 capped it at fifteen players, patch 1.10.0 at ten, and there it stayed.
The five-player cap arrived with Cataclysm.
The LBRS everybody remembers is a later game.

cards.subject: An orc here is the traitor in the room
lines: Rend calls himself Warchief of the true Horde — orcs, forest trolls, ogres and goblins who refused Thrall and kept the old bloodlust.
The actual authority is Nefarian, who runs them as a private army.
Both factions are unwelcome, for opposite reasons.

cards.subject: One of the mobs is a red dragon
lines: On a platform above the city stands what reads as an ordinary Scarshield Infiltrator. Walk up to him carrying an Unadorned Seal of Ascension and he drops the disguise.
He is Vaelastrasz, in mortal shape.
"Your search could take decades."

cards.subject: The key is forged in a swamp
lines: Three gemstones, one off each clan's boss. Then you leave the mountain entirely.
The seal is finished in Dustwallow Marsh, by beating a black drake down, mind-controlling him and making him breathe on it.
The ring is what lets a thing that is not a dragon walk past Nefarian's wards.

cards.subject: You summon a boss by putting a head on a spike
lines: Kill Highlord Omokk and take his head. Pull a Roughshod Pike off the east wall of upper Hordemar. Carry both to the ogre platform and mount the one on the other.
The ogres answer in waves. Then Urok comes.
Only one head drops per run.

cards.subject: The pikes are on the wall beside sleeping orcs
lines: The Scarshield Legionnaires stationed around them are asleep.
You lift a pike off the wall next to one of them.
Whether he stays asleep is up to you.

cards.subject: Something is very, very angry
lines: Halycon is a huge worg denned with a brood of pups. She and Gizrul are how the Dark Horde breeds its attack worgs.
Kill her and the game tells the whole instance: "A horrifying howl can be heard echoing through the halls of Blackrock Spire."
That is her mate, and he is coming.

cards.subject: The rare that made blacksmiths camp a dungeon
lines: A Firebrand Legion champion standing among the orcs in the lowest part of Hordemar, and he does not always spawn.
He carries Plans: Arcanite Reaper.
That single sheet of paper is why some people ran this place over and over without caring about the seal at all.

cards.subject: Six neighbourhoods for one dungeon
lines: Chamber of Battle, Halycon's Lair, Mok'Doom, Skitterweb Tunnels, the Storehouse, Tazz'Alor.
Between the orc barracks and the ogre platform the place stops being a city and turns into a spider hole.
It is the only stretch in here that is not somebody's army.

cards.subject: There is a dead adventurer in Voone's room
lines: A tauren druid who fell into the lower Spire fleeing spectral assassins, survived the fall, and was tortured by the trolls and by Voone before they finished him.
You summon him back with a brazier in the same room he was held in.
He fights you shifting through bear, cat and sprite darter.

cards.subject: The last boss is not an orc
lines: The end of the orc city is a black dragonspawn, placed here by Nefarian's chain of command and taking orders from the general upstairs.
He has no love for the Dark Horde he supervises.
At half health he calls for help and gets one of each clan.

cards.subject: The far end is not in here
lines: A ledge above the city, three gemstones, a dragon in a swamp — and a door upstairs you still cannot open.
This whole dungeon is the lock on the next one.
